newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico trade surplus for February $264 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico trade surplus for February $264 mln.

text.p: Mexico's preliminary trade surplus for February was $264 million, making a total surplus estimated at $724 million for the first two months of the year, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a surplus of $292 million in February.
Exports in February were $8.061 billion, 13.3 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
For the first two months of the year, exports were $16.186 billion, 13.5 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
Imports in February were $7.797 billion, 17.7 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
For the first two months of 1997, imports were 15.462 billion, 18.1 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
Exports of manufactured products, were $6.647 billion in February, 13.3 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
In the first two months of the year exports of manufactured goods was $13.248 billion, 12.4 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
In February, exports from the petroleum sector were $899 million, 17.2 percent higher than in February 1996.
In the first two months of the year exports of petroleum products were $1.974 billion, 25.6 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
In February, the value of agricultural products exports totalled $475 million, 7.5 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
Exports of mining goods in Febraury were $40 million, or 8.4 percent higher than in February 1996.
In January and February, mining exports rose 1.5 percent from the same period a year earlier.
In February, manufactured goods exports made up 81.8 percent of the total, petroleum products 12.2 percent, agriculture 5.5 percent and mining 0.5 percent, the ministry said.
In February, imports of intermediate goods were $6.266 billion, 16.6 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
In the first two months of the year, imports of intermediate goods were $12.323 billion, 16.1 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
Imports of capital goods were $962 million in February, 28.6 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
Imports of capital goods were $2.017 billion in the first two months of the year, 31.3 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
Imports of consumer goods were $569 million in February, 14.3 percent higher than in the same month a year earlier.
In the first two months of the year, imports of consumer goods were $1.122 billiion, 18.3 percent higher than in the same period a year earlier.
